nodes.name: Introduce the event $\Omega_\l$
nodes.statement: To upper bound the three terms of the right hand side, we introduce the event \begin{equation} \Omega_\l = \Big\{\|\bL(\bxi_J) \|_2^2\le 2|J|(p+\l |J|)\text{ for all } J\subseteq [n]\Big\}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Define the uniform noise-control event $\Omega_\l$ over all subsets $J\subseteq[n]$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: State the three claims
nodes.statement: We will show that the following three claims are true for the tuning parameter $\l$ chosen as in the statement of the theorem. \begin{description}\itemsep=5pt \item[Claim 1:] On the event $\Omega_\l$, at least half of the elements of each $\hat J_\ell$ belong to the true sparsity pattern $S$. Thus $|\hat S|\le 2s$. \item[Claim 2:] $\|\bL(\bfY_{S\setminus\hat S})\|_2^2\le 12\sigma^2 s(p+\l s)$. \item[Claim 3:] The probability of $\Omega_\l$ is close to $1$. \end{description}
nodes.statement_short: Announce Claims 1-3 that drive the argument.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Claims imply the theorem
nodes.statement: Let us first show that these claims imply the claim of the theorem. Indeed, the second term of the right hand side of \eqref{line:3} is bounded by $\sigma\sqrt{12s(p+\l s)}$ in view of Claim 2. The third term is bounded by $\sigma\sqrt{2s(p+\l s)}$ on the event $\O_\l$. Concerning the first term, we know that on $\O_\l$ it is bounded by $\sigma\sqrt{2|\hat S|(p+\l |\hat S|)}$. In view of Claim 1, $|\hat S|\le 2s$. All these inequalities imply that \begin{align} \|\hat\bL{}^{\rm GSS}-\bL(\bfT)\|_2^2 &\le 60\sigma^2{s(p+\l s)} \end{align} on the event $\O_\l$. This is exactly the claim of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the three bounds to get $60\sigma^2 s(p+\l s)$ on $\Omega_\l$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1
nodes.statement: Let us prove now Claims 1-3. To prove the first claim, let us assume that there is a set $J$ among $\hat J_1,\ldots,\hat J_\ell$ and a subset $J_0\subset J$ of cardinality\footnote{To avoid uninteresting and irrelevant technicalities, we assume here that $|J|$ is even.} $|J|/2$ such that $J_0\subset S^c$. This readily implies that $\|\bL(\bfY_{J})\|_2^2\ge 12\sigma^2 |J|(p+\l |J|)$ and $\|\bL(\bfY_{J\setminus J_0})\|_2^2< 6\sigma^2 |J|(p+\l |J|/2)$. Using the additivity of $\bL$ and the triangle inequality, we get \begin{align} \|\bL(\bfY_{J})\|_2^2 & \le (\|\bL(\bfY_{J\setminus J_0})\|_2+ \sigma\|\bL(\bxi_{J_0})\|_2)^2 \phantom{\frac32} \\ & \le \frac32\|\bL(\bfY_{J\setminus J_0})\|_2^2+ 3\sigma^2\|\bL(\bxi_{J_0})\|_2^2\\ & < 9\sigma^2 |J|(p+\l |J|/2)+ 3\sigma^2 |J|(p+\l|J|/2) \phantom{\frac32}\\ & < 12\sigma^2 |J|(p+\l|J|). \phantom{\frac32} \end{align} This is in contradiction with the fact that $J$ is one of the sets $\hat J_1,\ldots,\hat J_L$. So, Claim 1 is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Assume half of a selected set lies outside $S$ and derive a contradiction with its selection.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 2
nodes.statement: The proof of Claim 2 is simpler. By construction, the set $S\setminus \hat S$ is a subset of $I_L$, where $L$ is the number of steps performed by the algorithm. Since the algorithm terminated after the $L$th step, this means that $\calI$ was empty, which implies that $\|\bL(\bfY_{S\setminus\hat S})\|_2^2\le 12\sigma^2 |S\setminus\hat S|(p+\l|S\setminus\hat S|) \le 12\sigma^2 s(p+\l s)$.
nodes.statement_short: The missed support lies in the final $I_L$, on which the selection criterion failed.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3
nodes.statement: It remains to prove Claim 3. This can be done using the union bound and tail bounds for $\chi^2_p$-distributed random variables. Indeed, we have \begin{align} \prob_\bfT\big(\Omega_\lambda^c\big) &\le \sum_{k=1}^n \prob_\bfT\big(\exists J\subset [n]\text{ s.t. } |J|=k\text{ and } \|\bL(\bxi_J)\|_2^2> 2|J|(p+\l|J|)\big)\\ &\le \sum_{k=1}^n {{n}\choose{k}} \max_{J:|J|=k} \prob_\bfT\big(\|\bL(\bxi_J)\|_2^2> 2k(p+\l k)\big)\\ &\le \sum_{k=1}^n {{n}\choose{k}} \prob\big(\eta > 2p + 2 \l k\big) \end{align} where $\eta\sim \chi^2_p$. Using the well known bound on the tails of the $\chi^2_p$ distribution, we get \begin{align} \prob\big(\Omega_\lambda^c\big) &\le \sum_{k=1}^n {{n}\choose{k}} e^{-2\l k/3} = (1+e^{-2\l/3})^n-1. \end{align} Therefore, for $\lambda = \nicefrac32\log(\nicefrac{2n}{\delta})$, we obtain that $\prob_\bfT\big(\Omega_\lambda^c\big)\le \delta$. This completes the proof of Claim~3 and of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: A union bound over subsets plus the $\chi^2_p$ tail gives $\prob(\Omega_\l^c)\le\delta$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Decompose the error
nodes.statement: Recall that $\bXi =(\bxi_1, \ldots,\bxi_n)$. First, we decompose \begin{align} \hat{\bL}{}^{\rm GHT}-\bL(\bfT) &= \bL(\bY_S-\bTheta) - \bL(\bY_{S\setminus S_\lambda} )+ \bL(\bY_{S_\l\setminus S})\\ &= \sigma\bL(\bXi_S) - \bL(\bY_{S\setminus S_\lambda} )+ \sigma\bL(\bXi_{S_\l\setminus S})\\ &= \sigma\bL(\bXi_{S\cap S_\lambda}) - \bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda} )+ \sigma\bL(\bXi_{S_\l\setminus S}). \end{align} so that \begin{align} \big\| \hat{\bL}{}^{\rm GHT}-\bL(\bfT) \big\|_2 &\le \sigma\|\bL(\bXi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2 + \|\bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\|_2 + \sigma\|\bL(\bXi_{S_\l \setminus S})\|_2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Write the error as stochastic error on $S\cap S_\lambda$, bias on $S\setminus S_\lambda$ and noise on $S_\l\setminus S$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Bound the stochastic error via the spectral norm
nodes.statement: The first term corresponds to the stochastic error of estimating the signal vectors that are correctly identified as nonzero. We can write \begin{equation} \|\bL(\bXi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2 = \|\bXi_{S}\mathbf 1_{S\cap S_\lambda}\|_2\le \sqrt{s}\|\bXi_{S}\|. \end{equation} The second-order moment of the spectral norm of the random matrix $\bXi_S$ can be evaluated using well-known upper bounds on the spectral norm of matrices with independent Gaussian entries, recalled in \Cref{lemma_Wishart2} below, so that \begin{equation} \esp_\bfT \big[\|\bL(\bXi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2^2\big] \le 3s^2 + 3sp+12s. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Use $\|\bL(\bXi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2\le\sqrt s\|\bXi_S\|$ and the Wishart spectral-norm bound.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Bound the approximation error on the support
nodes.statement: Set $\eta_i=\btheta_i^\top\bxi_i/\|\btheta_i\|_2$. We can control the second term in \eqref{ineq:2} using the following inequality \begin{align} \|\bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\|_2&\le \sum_{i\in S} \|\bt_i\|_2 \fcar_{\|\bt_i\|^2<\lambda^2 -2\sigma\bt_i^\top \bxi_i-\sigma^2\|\bxi_i\|^2} \\ &\le s(\lambda^2-\sigma^2p)^{1/2}+2\sigma\sum_{i\in S} |\eta_i| + \sigma\sum_{i\in S} \big| \|\bxi_i\|^2-p\, \big|^{1/2}. \end{align} This readily yields \begin{equation} \esp_\bfT \big[\|\bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\|_2^2]^{1/2} \le s(\lambda^2-\sigma^2p)^{1/2}+2\sigma s + \sigma s (2p)^{1/4}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Control $\|\bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\|_2$ by $s(\lambda^2-\sigma^2p)^{1/2}+2\sigma s+\sigma s(2p)^{1/4}$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Bound the Type II error off the support
nodes.statement: The third term in \eqref{ineq:2} corresponds to the Type II error in the problem of support estimation. Denoting $t=(\lambda^2-\sigma^2p)/\sigma^2$, and using tail bounds for the chi-squared random variables (see \Cref{lemme_esperancechideux} below), we get \begin{align} \esp_\bfT[\|\bXi_{S_\l \setminus S}\|_2^2] &= \esp_\bfT\bigg[\bigg\| \sum_{i\in S^c} \bxi_i\fcar(\|\bxi_i\|_2\ge \l/\s)\bigg\|_2^2\bigg]\\ &= \sum_{i\in S^c}\esp_\bfT[\|\bxi_i\|_2^2\fcar(\|\bxi_i\|_2^2\ge p+t)]\\ &\le 2n \big( pe^{-t^2/32p}\,\fcar_{t< 4p} + t e^{-t/4}\fcar_{t \ge 4p}\big). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the truncated $\chi^2$ moment bound to the falsely retained columns.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Substitute the choice of the threshold
nodes.statement: Using the fact that $t= 4\log(1+n/s^2)\vee\big\{16p\log(1+n^2p/s^4)\big\}^{1/2}$ we arrive at \begin{align} \esp_\bfT[\|\bXi_{S_\l \setminus S}\|_2^2] &\le \Big(8s^2\log(1+n/s^2)\Big)\vee \Big(2s^2\sqrt{p} \wedge 2np\Big). \end{align} The result follows from the previous upper bounds and the choice of $\l$.
nodes.statement_short: Plug in $t$ to obtain the $8s^2\log(1+n/s^2)\vee(2s^2\sqrt p\wedge 2np)$ bound.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Least favourable configuration and decomposition
nodes.statement: We define $\bfT$ as the matrix with entries $\e=\sigma p^{-1/4}$ in the first $s$ columns and $0$ elsewhere. Using the inequality $\forall a,b,~(a-b)^2\ge a^2/2-b^2$ and~\eqref{decomposition}, we get \begin{align} \esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \hat{\bL}{}^{\rm GHT}-\bL(\bfT) \big\|_2^2 \big] &\ge \frac12 \esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \sigma\bL(\bXi_{S_\l\setminus S}) - \bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big] - \sigma^2\esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \bL(\bXi_{S\cap S_\lambda}) \big\|_2^2\big]. \end{align} Moreover, $\bL(\bXi_{S_\l\setminus S})$ being centered and independent of $\bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})$, we can develop \begin{align} \esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \sigma\bL(\bXi_{S_\l\setminus S}) - \bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big] &= \sigma^2\esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \bL(\bXi_{S_\l\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] + \esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big]. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\bfT$ with $s$ columns of entries $\sigma p^{-1/4}$ and separate the bias and noise contributions.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Case $\lambda^2\ge\sigma^2p+\sigma^2\sqrt p$
nodes.statement: First assume that $\lambda^2\ge \sigma^2 p + \sigma^2\sqrt{p}$ and focus on the second term in the right-hand side of the last display. Using Jensen's inequality, we have \begin{align} \esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big\|_2^2\big] &\ge \big\| \esp_\bfT \big[\bL(\bTheta_{S\setminus S_\lambda})\big]\big\|_2^2\\ &= p\e^2s^2 \max_{i\in S}\prob_\bfT\big(\|\bY_i\|_2<\l\big)^2\\ &= s^2\sqrt{p}\max_{i\in S} \prob_\bfT\big(\|\bY_i\|_2<\l\big)^2. \end{align} On the other hand, since $\sgn(\bxi_i^\top\btheta_i)$ is a Rademacher random variable independent of $\|\bxi_i\|_2^2$, for every $i\in S$, we have \begin{equation} \prob_\bfT\big(\|\bY_i\|_2^2<\lambda^2\big) \ge 0.5\prob\big(\sigma^2\|\bxi_1\|_2^2-\sigma^2p<\sigma^2\sqrt{p}-p\e^2\big) = 0.5\prob\big(\|\bxi_1\|_2^2-p<0\big). \end{equation} This last probability converges to $1/2$, so that it is larger than $1/4$ for all $p$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: Jensen plus a Rademacher symmetry argument give $s^2\sqrt p$ from the missed signals.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Case $\lambda^2<\sigma^2p+\sigma^2\sqrt p$
nodes.statement: In the other case, $\lambda^2< \sigma^2 p + \sigma^2\sqrt{p}$, we consider the first term: \begin{align} \esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \bL(\bXi_{S_\l\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] &= (n-s)p - (n-s)\esp [\|\bxi_1\|_2^2 \fcar_{\|\bxi_1\|_2\le\l/\sigma}] \\ &\ge (n-s)p - (n-s)(p+\sqrt{p}) \prob\big(\|\bxi_1\|_2^2-p\le\sqrt{p}\big). \end{align} The probability in the right-hand side converges to $\Phi(2^{-1/2})\le 0.8$, so that for $p\ge 64$ and $s\le n/2$, we have \begin{equation} \esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \bL(\bXi_{S_\l\setminus S})\big\|_2^2\big] \ge (n-s) (0.2p-0.8p^{1/2}) \ge 0.05 np. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A small threshold lets through $\Omega(np)$ of pure noise.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Subtract the stochastic term
nodes.statement: Finally, according to \eqref{esperance_norm}, we have for $p$ large enough \begin{align} \esp_\bfT \big[\|\bL(\bXi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2^2\big] \le 3s^2 + 3sp+12s \le \frac{s^2\sqrt{p}}{65} + 3sp \end{align} so that \begin{equation} \esp_\bfT \big[\big\| \hat{\bL}{}^{\rm GHT}-\bL(\bfT) \big\|_2^2\big] \ge \frac{s^2\sqrt{p}}{65}\wedge(0.05np) - 3sp. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Absorb $\esp[\|\bL(\bXi_{S\cap S_\lambda})\|_2^2]$ into $s^2\sqrt p/65+3sp$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Combine the two regimes
nodes.statement: We have to distinguish between two cases. If $s^2\sqrt{p}\le 196sp$, then the result holds in view of~\Cref{theorem_lowerbound}. In the opposite case, the result holds as long as $s\le n/61$.
nodes.statement_short: Fall back on the minimax lower bound when $s^2\sqrt p\le 196sp$, else use $s\le n/61$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Three-term decomposition
nodes.statement: To ease notation, for every random vector $X$ we write $\|X\|_{L_2}$ for $(\esp[\|X\|_2^2])^{1/2}$. We first notice that \begin{align} \hat{\bL}{}^{\rm GST}-\bL(\bTheta) &= \sum_{i\in S} \bt_i \bigg\{\bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma} {(\|\bY_i\|^2_2-\sigma^2p)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+-1\bigg\} \qquad &(:=T_1)\\ &+ \sigma\sum_{i\in S} \bxi_i \bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma}{\big(\|\bY_i\|^2_2-\sigma^2p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+ \qquad &(:=T_2)\\ &+ \sigma\sum_{i\not\in S} \bxi_i \bigg(1-\frac{\sigma\gamma}{\sigma\big(\|\bxi_i\|^2_2-p\big)_+^{1/2}}\bigg)_+\qquad &(:=T_3), \end{align} so that we only need to bound the expected squared norms of the three terms in the right-hand side. These three terms have the following meanings: the first one is the bias of estimation or the approximation error, the second term is the stochastic error on the support $S$, whereas the third term is the stochastic error on $S^\complement$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $T_1,T_2,T_3$: bias, stochastic error on $S$, stochastic error off $S$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Evaluation of the approximation error
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Evaluation of the approximation error} For the first term, we use the Minkowski inequality as follows \begin{align} \|T_1\|_{L_2}\le \Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \bt_i \fcar_{\|\bY_i\|_2^2\le\sigma^2 (p+\gamma^2) }\Big\|_{L_2} + \sigma\Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \bt_i \frac{\gamma\,\fcar_{\|\bY_i\|_2^2>\sigma^2 (p+\gamma^2)}}{\big(\|\bY_i\|^2_2-\sigma^2p\big)^{1/2}}\Big\|_{L_2}. \end{align} The first part can be treated exactly as in \eqref{eval_on_support} of the proof of~\Cref{theorem_HT}, \ie \begin{equation} \Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \bt_i \fcar_{\|\bY_i\|_2^2\le\sigma^2 (p+\gamma^2) }\Big\|_{L_2} \le \sigma s \big(\gamma+2 + (2p)^{1/4}\big). \end{equation} For assessing the second term in the right hand side of \eqref{eqT1}, we set \begin{align} T_{1,i} = \frac{\|\bt_i\|_2\gamma\,\fcar_{\|\bY_i\|_2^2>\sigma^2 (p+\gamma^2)}} {(\|\bt_i\|^2_2+2\sigma\bt_i^\top\bxi_i+\sigma^2\big(\|\bxi_i\|_2^2-p\big))^{1/2}} . \end{align} We consider two cases. The first case corresponds to $\big|2\sigma\bt_i^\top\bxi_i+\sigma^2\big(\|\bxi_i\|_2^2-p\big)\big|<\|\bt_i\|_2^2/2$. In this case one easily checks that $T_{1,i}\le \sqrt{2}\,\gamma$. In the second case, $\big|2\sigma\bt_i^\top\bxi_i+\sigma^2\big(\|\bxi_i\|_2^2-p\big)\big|\ge\|\bt_i\|_2^2/2$, we have \begin{equation} \|\bt_i\|_2^2/4 \le 2\s|\bt_i^\top\bxi_i| \quad \text{or} \quad \|\bt_i\|_2^2/4 \le \sigma^2\big|\|\bxi_i\|_2^2-p\big|. \end{equation} This readily implies that \begin{equation} T_{1,i}= \frac{\|\bt_i\|\gamma\,\fcar_{\|\bY_i\|_2^2>\sigma^2 (p+\gamma^2)}} {\big(\|\bY_i\|^2_2-\sigma^2p\big)^{1/2}}\le \|\bt_i\| \le 8\sigma \frac{|\bt_i^\top\bxi_i|}{\|\bt_i\|_2}+ 2\sigma\sqrt{|\|\bxi_i\|_2^2-p|}. \end{equation} Therefore, using the fact that $\esp[|\bt_i^\top\bxi_i|^2] = \|\bt_i\|_2^2$ and $\esp[|\|\bxi_i\|_2^2-p|^2] = 2p$, we get \begin{equation} \|T_{1,i}\|_{L_2} \le 8\sigma + 2\sigma (2p)^{1/4}. \end{equation} Combining this inequality with \eqref{eqT1} and \eqref{eqT1a}, we arrive at \begin{align} \|T_1\|_{L_2} &\le \sigma s\gamma+2\sigma s + \sigma s(2p)^{1/4} + 8\sigma s+ 2\sigma s(2p)^{1/4}\\ &= \sigma s\gamma+10\sigma s + 3\sigma s(2p)^{1/4}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Minkowski's inequality and a two-case analysis give $\|T_1\|_{L_2}\le\sigma s\gamma+10\sigma s+3\sigma s(2p)^{1/4}$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Evaluation of the stochastic error on $S$
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Evaluation of the stochastic error on $S$} The second term can be treated exactly as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem_HT} using Wishart matrices, \ie \begin{equation} \|T_2\|_{L_2}^2 \le \sigma^2 s\esp[\|\bXi_S\|^2] \le \sigma^2(3s^2+3sp+12s). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Reuse the Wishart spectral-norm bound to get $\|T_2\|_{L_2}^2\le\sigma^2(3s^2+3sp+12s)$.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Evaluation of the stochastic error off $S$
nodes.statement:
\paragraph{Evaluation of the stochastic error on $S^\complement$} For the third term, we write  egin{align} \|T_3\|_{L_2}^2=\sigma^2 igg\| \sum_{i
ot\in S}  xi_i  igg(1- rac{\gamma}{ ig(\| xi_i\|^2_2-p ig)_+^{1/2}} igg)_+ igg\|_{L_2}^2 &= \sigma^2\sum_{i
ot\in S}  igg\| xi_i igg(1- rac{\gamma}{(\| xi_i\|^2_2 -p)_+^{1/2}} igg)_+ igg\|_{L_2}^2\ &\le \sigma^2\sum_{i
ot\in S} \esp ig[\| xi_i\|_2^2  car_{\| xi_i\|_2^2> p+ \gamma^2} ig]. \end{align} We conclude by~\Cref{lemme_esperancechideux} that the last term satisfies  egin{equation} \|T_3\|_{L_2}^2\le 2n\sigma^2  ig( pe^{-\gamma^4/32p}\, car_{\gamma^2< 4p} + \gamma^2e^{-\gamma^2/4} car_{\gamma^2\ge 4p} ig). \end{equation} Using the fact that $\gamma^2= 4\log(1+n/s^2)\vee ig\{16p\log(1+n^2p/s^4)  ig\}^{1/2}$ we arrive at  egin{align} \|T_3\|_{L_2}^2 &\le \sigma^2 \Big(8s^2\log(1+n/s^2)\Big)\vee \Big(2s^2\sqrt{p} \wedge 2np\Big). \end{align} This completes the proof of the theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Independence plus the truncated $\chi^2$ moment bound give the $s^2\sqrt p\wedge np$ term.
nodes.section: 5.1 Proofs of the theorems of Section 2

nodes.name: Basic inequality
nodes.statement: In view of~\eqref{definition_groupestimator}, we have \begin{equation} \big\| (\bTheta-\hat{\bTheta})\bfPi + \sigma\bXi\bfPi \big\|_F^2 + \l \sum_{i=1}^n \|\hat\bt_i\|_2 \le \sigma^2 \| \bXi\bfPi \|_F^2 + \l \sum_{i=1}^n \|\bt_i\|_2. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Optimality of $\hat\bTheta$ gives the basic inequality of the penalized problem.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Expand the left-hand side
nodes.statement: Developing the left-hand side, this yields \begin{align} \| (\bTheta-\hat{\bTheta})\bfPi \|_F^2 &\le 2\sigma\sum_{n=1}^n (\bXi\bfPi)_i^\top(\hat\bt_i-\bt_i) + \l \sum_{i=1}^n \big\{ \|\bt_i\|_2 - \|\hat\bt_i\|_2\big\}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Expand to a noise cross-term plus the penalty difference.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz on the event $\mathcal A$
nodes.statement: Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have on the event \begin{equation} \mathcal{A} = \Big\{ \max_{i\in [n]} \big\| (\bXi\bfPi)_i \big\|_2 \le \frac{\lambda}{4\sigma} \Big\} \end{equation} that \begin{align} \|(\bTheta-\hat{\bTheta})\bfPi\|_F^2 &\le \frac\l2 \sum_{i=1}^n \Big\{ \|\hat\bt_i-\bt_i\|_2 + 2 \|\bt_i\|_2 - 2 \|\hat\bt_i\|_2 \Big\} \\ &\le \frac{3\lambda}2 \sum_{i\in S} \|\hat\bt_i-\bt_i\|_2 - \frac\l2 \sum_{i\not\in S} \|\hat\bt_i-\bt_i\|_2, \end{align} where we used the triangular inequality.
nodes.statement_short: On $\mathcal A=\{\max_i\|(\bXi\bfPi)_i\|_2\le\lambda/4\sigma\}$ the noise term is absorbed by the penalty.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Derive the cone condition
nodes.statement: The last inequality implies that \begin{align} \sum_{i\not\in S} \|\hat\bt_i-\bt_i\|_2\le 3\sum_{i\in S} \|\hat\bt_i-\bt_i\|_2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Off-support mass is at most three times the on-support mass.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Apply the projection lemma
nodes.statement: Furthermore, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we get \begin{equation} \|(\bTheta-\hat\bTheta)\bfPi\|_F^2 \le \frac{3\lambda}2 \sqrt{s} \|\bTheta-\hat\bTheta\|_F. \end{equation} We can then apply Lemma~\ref{lemme_Pi}, since~(\ref{theoreme_bornesuperieure1_2}) ensures that the condition is satisfied with $a=3$: provided that $s\le n/16$, we have \begin{equation} \frac12 \|\hat\bTheta-\bTheta\|_F^2 \le \frac{3\lambda}2 \sqrt{s} \|\hat\bTheta-\bTheta\|_F, \end{equation} so that \begin{equation} \|\hat\bTheta-\bTheta\|_F \le 3 \l \sqrt{s}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma on $\bfPi$ with $a=3$ and $s\le n/16$ gives $\|\hat\bTheta-\bTheta\|_F\le3\l\sqrt s$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Transfer the bound to $\hat\bmu$
nodes.statement: The first claim follows now from~\Cref{lemme_probabiliteA}. To show the second inequality, it suffices to remark that \begin{align} \|\hat\bmu-\bmu\|_2^2 & \le \frac2{n^2}\|(\hat\bTheta-\bTheta)\mathbf 1_n\|_2^2 +2\sigma^2\|\bL_n(\bXi)\|_2^2\\ & \le \frac{2}{n^2}\bigg(\sum_{i\in [n]}\|\hat\btheta_i-\btheta_i\|_2\bigg)^2 +2\sigma^2\|\bL_n(\bXi)\|_2^2\\ & \le \frac{2}{n^2}\bigg(4\sum_{i\in S}\|\hat\btheta_i-\btheta_i\|_2\bigg)^2 +2\sigma^2\|\bL_n(\bXi)\|_2^2\\ & \le \frac{32s}{n^2}\sum_{i\in S}\|\hat\btheta_i-\btheta_i\|_2^2 +2\sigma^2\|\bL_n(\bXi)\|_2^2\\ & \le \frac{288s^2\lambda^2}{n^2} +2\sigma^2\|\bL_n(\bXi)\|_2^2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Chain the cone condition and Cauchy-Schwarz to reach $288s^2\lambda^2/n^2$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Control the Gaussian average
nodes.statement: To complete the proof, we use the fact that $n\|\bL_n(\bXi)\|_2^2$ is a $\chi^2(p)$ random variable, which implies that with probability at least $1-\d/2$ it is bounded from above by $2p+4\log(2/\delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: $n\|\bL_n(\bXi)\|_2^2\sim\chi^2(p)$ is at most $2p+4\log(2/\delta)$ with probability $1-\d/2$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Notation and centred decomposition
nodes.statement: To ease notation, we set $\sigma_{n,p}^2 = (n-1)\sigma^2p/n$, $w_i=\big( 1-\sigma\gamma/\sqrt{(\|\bZ_i \|_2^2-\sigma_{n,p}^2)_+} \big)_+$, $\tilde\bDelta_n = \tilde\bL_n-\bL_n(\bTheta)$ and $\bar\bxi_i= \bxi_i-\bar\bxi$. Then, \begin{equation} \bZ_i = \bt_i + \tilde\bDelta_n + \sigma\bar\bxi_i. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Write $\bZ_i=\bt_i+\tilde\bDelta_n+\sigma\bar\bxi_i$ and define the weights $w_i$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Weights vanish off the support
nodes.statement: We first show that with high probability the weights $w_i$ vanish outside the support $S$.
nodes.statement_short: Announce the lemma stating $w_i=0$ for $i\not\in S$ on $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Reduce the sum to the support
nodes.statement: Using equation~\eqref{Z0} and the fact that $w_i=0$ for every $i\not\in S$ in the event $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$, we get \begin{align} \bL(\hat{\bTheta}-\bTheta) &= \sum_{i=1}^n \bZ_i w_i-\sum_{i\in S} \bt_i = \sum_{i\in S} \big(\bZ_i w_i -\bt_i\big). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Only indices in $S$ contribute to $\bL(\hat\bTheta-\bTheta)$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Triangle inequality split
nodes.statement: Replacing $\bZ_i$ by $\bt_i + \tilde\bDelta_n + \sigma\bar\bxi_i$ and using the triangle inequality, we obtain \begin{align} \|\bL(\hat{\bTheta}-\bTheta) \|_2 &\le \Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \big(\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\big) (w_i-1)\Big\|_2 + \Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \big(\bZ_i-\bt_i\big)+\sigma\bar\bxi_i(w_i-1)\Big\|_2\\ &\le \sum_{i\in S} \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2 |w_i-1| + \Big\|\sum_{i\in S} \big(\tilde\bDelta_n + \sigma\bar\bxi_i w_i\big)\Big\|_2\\ &\le \sum_{i\in S} \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2 |w_i-1| + {s}\big\|\tilde\bDelta_n\big\|_2 + \sigma\Big\|\sum_{i\in S}\bar\bxi_i w_i\Big\|_2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Split into a shrinkage term, $s\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2$, and a weighted noise term.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Announce the evaluation of the two terms
nodes.statement: We will now evaluate the first and the third terms of the right-hand side.
nodes.statement_short: State that the first and third terms remain to be bounded.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Hölder bound on the cross term
nodes.statement: Let us introduce the $p\times s$ matrix $\bXi_S = [\,\bar\bxi_i; i\in S\,]$ (the matrix obtained by concatenating the vectors $\bar\bxi_i$ with subscript $i$ running over $S$). Using the H\"older inequality, one can check that \begin{align} \sum_{i\in S}\big\{2\s|\bar\bxi_i^\top\tilde\bDelta_n|\big\}^{1/2} &\le \sqrt{2\sigma}\, s^{3/4} \bigg(\sum_{i\in S} |\bar\bxi_i^\top\tilde\bDelta_n|^2 \bigg)^{1/4}\\ &= \sqrt{2\sigma}\, s^{3/4} \|\bXi_S^\top\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2^{1/2}\\ &\le \sqrt{2\sigma}\, s^{3/4} \|\bXi_S\|^{1/2}\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2^{1/2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Hölder's inequality gives $\sqrt{2\sigma}s^{3/4}\|\bXi_S\|^{1/2}\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2^{1/2}$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Bound the weighted noise term
nodes.statement: Finally, the third term in the right-hand side of \eqref{Z1} can be bounded as follows: \begin{equation} \Big\| \sum_{i\in S}\bar\bxi_iw_i\Big\|_2 = \|\bXi_S \bsw\|_2\le \sqrt{s}\,\|\bXi_S\|. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\|\sum_{i\in S}\bar\bxi_iw_i\|_2\le\sqrt s\,\|\bXi_S\|$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Combine the bounds
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{Z1}, \eqref{Z2}, \eqref{Z3} and \eqref{Z4}, we arrive at \begin{align} \|\bL(\hat{\bTheta}-\bTheta) \|_2 &\le 2\sigma\sum_{i\in S}\big(|\eta_i| + \big\{2\s|\tilde\bDelta_n^\top \bar\bxi_i|\big\}^{1/2}\big) +1.96\,\sigma s\gamma + {s}\big\|\tilde\bDelta_n\big\|_2 + \sigma\sqrt{s}\,\|\bXi_S\|\\ &\le 2\sigma\sum_{i\in S}|\eta_i|+2.21\,\sigma s\g+\sqrt{2\sigma}\, s^{3/4} \|\bXi_S\|^{1/2} \big\|\tilde\bDelta_n\big\|_2^{1/2}+\sigma\sqrt{s}\,\|\bXi_S\|\\ &\le 2\sigma\sum_{i\in S}|\eta_i| +2.34\,\sigma s\gamma + 2\sigma\sqrt{s}\,\|\bXi_S\|. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Collect the terms into $2\sigma\sum_{i\in S}|\eta_i|+2.34\sigma s\gamma+2\sigma\sqrt s\|\bXi_S\|$.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Concentration events and conclusion
nodes.statement: According to \citep[Corollary~5.35]{vershynin_2012} (recalled in~\Cref{lemma_Wishart1} below for the reader's convenience) the event $\O_3 = \big\{ \|\bXi_S\| \le \sqrt{s}+\sqrt{p}+\{2\log(8/\delta)\}^{1/2} \big\}$ has probability at least $1-\delta/8$. One can also check that with probability at least $1-\delta/8$, the event $\Omega_4 = \{\sum_{i\in S}|\eta_i| \le s + \sqrt{s\log(8/\delta)}\}$ is realized. Assuming that $\delta\le 1/2$ so that $\log (8/\delta)\le (4/3)\log (4/\delta)$, this implies that in $\O_1\cap\bar\O$ with $\bar\O=\O_2\cap\O_3\cap\Omega_4$, we have \begin{align} \|\bL(\hat{\bTheta}-\bTheta) \|_2 &\le 4\sigma(\,s\gamma+ s + \sqrt{sp} + \{2s\log(4/\delta)\}^{1/2}). \end{align} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: On $\O_3\cap\Omega_4$ the spectral norm and the sum of $|\eta_i|$ concentrate, giving the stated bound.
nodes.section: 5.2 Proofs of the theorems of Section 3

nodes.name: Pythagorean identity
nodes.statement: We denote by $\bu_i\in\RR^n$ the column vector corresponding to the $i$-th row of $\bfU$. On the one hand, since $\nicefrac1n\bfJ_n$ is an orthogonal projection matrix, we have by the Pythagorean theorem \begin{align} \|\bfPi\bu^i\|_2^2 &= \|\bu^i\|_2^2 -\frac1{n^2} \|\bfJ_n\bu^i\|_2^2. \end{align} In particular, this implies that \begin{align} \|\bfU\bfPi\|_F^2 &= \|\bfU\|_F^2 -\frac1{n^2} \|\bfU\bfJ_n\|_F^2. \end{align}

nodes.name: Express $\|\bfU\bfJ_n\|_F$
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \begin{align} \|\bfU\bfJ_n\|_F &= \|\mathbf \bfU 1_n\mathbf 1_n^\top\|_F =\sqrt{n}\, \|\bfU \mathbf 1_n^\top\|_2 = \sqrt{n}\, \Big\|\sum_{i=1}^n \bu_i\Big\|_2 \le \sqrt{n}\, \sum_{i=1}^n \|\bu_i\|_2. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|\bfU\bfJ_n\|_F$ by $\sqrt n\sum_i\|\bu_i\|_2$.

nodes.name: Apply the cone condition
nodes.statement: Using \eqref{cone_cond} and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we get \begin{align} \sum_{i=1}^n \|\bu_i\|_2 &\le (1+a)\sum_{i\in S} \|\bu_i\|_2 \le (1+a)|S|^{1/2}\Big(\sum_{i\in S} \|\bu_i\|^2_2\Big)^{1/2} \le (1+a)|S|^{1/2}\|\bfU\|_F. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The cone condition and Cauchy-Schwarz give $\sum_i\|\bu_i\|_2\le(1+a)|S|^{1/2}\|\bfU\|_F$.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: This readily yields $\|\bfU\bfJ_n\|_F \le (1+a) (n|S|)^{1/2}\|\bfU\|_F$. Combining this inequality with \eqref{ineq:1}, we get the claim of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute into the Pythagorean identity.

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement: We prove by inductive reasoning that for every $k$ we have $\epsilon_k^2\le p$ and \eqref{recursion:claim}. This is trivially true for $k=0$.
nodes.statement_short: The claims hold trivially at $k=0$.

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: Assume that these claims hold true for some given value $k$. Let us check them for the value $k+1$. From recursion \eqref{eq:recursion}, one can infer that \begin{align} \epsilon_{k+1} \le \frac{16.5s}{n}(\epsilon_k\vee p^{1/4}\epsilon_k^{1/2}) +a \le \frac{33s}{n}(\epsilon_k\vee p^{1/4}\epsilon_k^{1/2})\vee 2a. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Simplify the recursion to $\epsilon_{k+1}\le\frac{33s}{n}(\epsilon_k\vee p^{1/4}\epsilon_k^{1/2})\vee2a$.

nodes.name: Close the induction
nodes.statement: The conditions of the lemma directly imply that $\epsilon_{k+1}^2\le p$. Therefore, \begin{align} \epsilon_{k+1} \le \frac{33sp^{1/4}\epsilon_k^{1/2}}{n}\vee 2a. \end{align} Applying inequality \eqref{recursion:claim}, we get the claim.
nodes.statement_short: $\epsilon_{k+1}^2\le p$ lets us apply the inductive bound and conclude.

nodes.name: Behaviour from a poor initialization
nodes.statement: One can note that even in the case $\epsilon_k>\sqrt{p}$, we get from \eqref{eq:recursion1a} that \begin{align} \epsilon_{k+1} \le \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_k +a. \end{align} Therefore, if the preliminary estimator is not good enough to guarantee that $\epsilon_0\le \sqrt{p}$, after a number of steps at most logarithmic in $\epsilon_0/(\sqrt{p}-2a)$, we will get an error $\epsilon_k$ smaller than $\sqrt{p}$.
nodes.statement_short: Even if $\epsilon_0>\sqrt p$, the halving recursion reaches $\sqrt p$ in logarithmically many steps.

nodes.name: Characterize positive weights
nodes.statement: It follows from the definition of $w_i$ that, for every $i\not\in S$, $w_i>0$ is equivalent to $$ \|\sigma\bar\bxi_i+\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2^2 > \sigma^2(p+\gamma^2). $$
nodes.statement_short: $w_i>0$ off $S$ means $\|\sigma\bar\bxi_i+\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2^2>\sigma^2(p+\gamma^2)$.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: In view of the triangle inequality, this implies that $$ \sigma\|\bar\bxi_i\|_2 + \|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2 > \sigma\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Split into $\sigma\|\bar\bxi_i\|_2+\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2>\sigma\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}$.

nodes.name: Substitute the event bounds
nodes.statement: In the event $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$, the last inequality implies $$ \sqrt{p+0.5\gamma^2} + \frac{\gamma^2}{4\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}}> \sqrt{p+\gamma^2}. $$
nodes.statement_short: On $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$ this becomes an inequality between explicit square roots.

nodes.name: Derive the contradiction
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that the last inequality is never true, implying thus that $w_i=0$. Indeed, \begin{align} \sqrt{p+\gamma^2} -\sqrt{p+0.5\gamma^2} & = \frac{0.5\gamma^2}{\sqrt{p+\gamma^2} +\sqrt{p+0.5\gamma^2}}\\ & > \frac{0.5\gamma^2}{\sqrt{p+\gamma^2} +\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}} = \frac{\gamma^2}{4\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: The gap $\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}-\sqrt{p+0.5\gamma^2}$ always exceeds $\gamma^2/4\sqrt{p+\gamma^2}$.

nodes.name: Probability of $\O_2$
nodes.statement: The fact that the probability of $\O_2$ is at least $1-\d/2$ is a consequence of the tail bound of a chi-squared random variable and the union bound.
nodes.statement_short: A $\chi^2$ tail bound and a union bound give $\prob(\O_2)\ge1-\d/2$.

nodes.name: Rewrite the discrepancy
nodes.statement: The definition of $\bZ_i$ yields \begin{align} \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2|w_i-1| &= \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2 \min\bigg\{ 1, \frac{\sigma\gamma}{\big(\|\bZ_i\|^2_2-\sigma_{n,p}^2\big)^{1/2}_+} \bigg\}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Write $\|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2|w_i-1|$ as a $\min\{1,\cdot\}$ expression.

nodes.name: Complete the square in the lower bound
nodes.statement: Let us introduce the random variables $\eta_i = \frac{n}{n-1}\bt_i^\top\bar\bxi_i/\|\bt_i\|_2$. It is clear that $\eta_i$ is Gaussian with zero mean and unit variance. Repeated use of the triangle inequality leads to \begin{align} \|\bZ_i\|_2^2 &\ge \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2 + \|\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2 + 2\sigma\bar\bxi_i^\top(\bt_i +\tilde\bDelta_n) \\ &\ge \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2 + \|\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\bt_i\|_2|\eta_i| +2\sigma\bar\bxi_i^\top\tilde\bDelta_n\\ &\ge \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2 + \|\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2 |\eta_i| -2\sigma\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2|\eta_i|+2\sigma\bar\bxi_i^\top\tilde\bDelta_n\\ &\ge (\|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2-\s|\eta_i|)^2 -\sigma^2\eta_i^2 + \|\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2 -2\sigma\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2|\eta_i|+2\sigma\bar\bxi_i^\top\tilde\bDelta_n. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Introduce standard Gaussians $\eta_i$ and lower bound $\|\bZ_i\|_2^2$ by a completed square.

nodes.name: Elementary inequality
nodes.statement: One can check the following simple fact: if $a,b,c,d>0$ then $$ a\min\Big(1,\frac{d}{\{(a-b)^2-c\}_+^{1/2}}\Big)\le b + d+\sqrt{c_+}. $$
nodes.statement_short: For positive $a,b,c,d$: $a\min(1,d/\{(a-b)^2-c\}_+^{1/2})\le b+d+\sqrt{c_+}$.

nodes.name: Substitute
nodes.statement: Taking in this inequality $a = \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2$, $c = \sigma^2\eta_i^2 - \|\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2 +2\sigma\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2|\eta_i|-2\sigma\bar\bxi_i^\top\tilde\bDelta_n + \sigma^2_{n,p}$, $b=\s|\eta_i|$ and $d=\sigma\g$, we arrive at \begin{align} \|\bZ_i-\sigma\bar\bxi_i\|_2|w_i-1| &\le 2\s|\eta_i| + \sigma\g+ \|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2\\ &\qquad+\sqrt{(\sigma_{n,p}^2-\sigma^2\|\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2)_+} +\sqrt{(2\sigma\bar\bxi_i^\top\tilde\bDelta_n -\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2^2)_+}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the inequality with the appropriate $a,b,c,d$.

nodes.name: Bound on the event
nodes.statement: In the event $\O_1\cap\O_2$, we upper bound $\|\tilde\bDelta_n\|_2$ and $|\sigma_{n,p}^2-\sigma^2\|\bar\bxi_i\|_2^2|$ respectively by $0.25\sigma\gamma$ and $0.5\sigma^2\gamma^2$. This leads to the claim of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: On $\O_1\cap\O_2$ bound the remaining terms by $0.25\sigma\gamma$ and $0.5\sigma^2\gamma^2$.

nodes.name: Case $x\ge 4d$
nodes.statement: First assume that $x\ge 4d$. Combining the relation \begin{align} \esp\big(\eta\, \fcar_{\eta\ge d+x}\big) &= (d+x)\prob(\eta\ge d+x)+\int_x^\pinf \prob(\eta\ge d+t)\,dt \end{align} with Lemma~\ref{lemme_chideux}, we get \begin{align} \esp\big(\eta\, \fcar_{\eta\ge d+x}\big) &\le (d+x) e^{-x/4} + \int_x^\pinf e^{-t/4}\, dt\\ &\le (4+d+x)e^{-x/4}\le (4d+x)e^{-x/4}\le 2xe^{-x/4}. \phantom{\int_0^\pinf} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the tail bound to get $(4d+x)e^{-x/4}\le2xe^{-x/4}$.

nodes.name: Case $x<4d$
nodes.statement: Now assume that $x<4d$. Then, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Lemma~\ref{lemme_chideux}, \begin{align} \esp\big(\eta\, \fcar_{\eta\ge d+x}\big) \le \sqrt{d(d+2)} e^{-x^2/32d}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz with the tail bound gives $\sqrt{d(d+2)}e^{-x^2/32d}$.

nodes.name: Distribution of the centred columns
nodes.statement: We first notice that \begin{equation} (\bXi\bfPi)_i = \bxi_i - \frac1n\sum_{j=1}^n \bxi_j\ \simiid\ \mathcal{N}\big(0,{\textstyle\frac{n-1}{n}}\bfI_p\big). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $(\bXi\bfPi)_i=\bxi_i-\frac1n\sum_j\bxi_j$ is $\mathcal N(0,\frac{n-1}{n}\bfI_p)$.

nodes.name: Apply the chi-squared tail
nodes.statement: This implies that the random variable $\big\|(\bXi\bfPi)_i\big\|_2^2$ is drawn from the $\frac{n-1}{n} \chi^2_p$ distribution, and the result follows from~\Cref{lemme_chideux}.
nodes.statement_short: The squared norm is $\frac{n-1}{n}\chi^2_p$; apply the tail bound and a union bound.

nodes.name: Integrate the tail
nodes.statement: It is clear that \begin{align} \esp[\|\bfA\|^2] &\le 3(N+n) + \int_0^\pinf \prob(\|\bfA\|^2>3(N+n)+x)\, dx \\ &\le 3(N+n) + 12\,\int_0^\pinf te^{-t^2/2}\, dt. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Write $\esp[\|\bfA\|^2]$ as $3(N+n)$ plus the integral of the tail probability.

nodes.name: Evaluate the integral
nodes.statement: The result follows from the fact that the last integral is equal to one.
nodes.statement_short: The integral equals one, giving $3N+3n+12$.
